title: Optimisation & Geometric Modelling: custom lesson practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values, configurations and requested results are original. Mapped Cambridge evidence informs lesson scope and reasoning structures only.

parts.prompt: The area $A\text{ m}^2$ of a rectangular enclosure is given by $A = 40x - 2x^2$ for $x > 0$. Find the value of $x$ that maximizes the area, and state the maximum area.
The perimeter $P\text{ cm}$ of a rectangle with fixed area $36\text{ cm}^2$ is given by $P = 2x + \dfrac{72}{x}$ for $x > 0$. Find the value of $x$ for which $P$ is a minimum.
A wire of length $24\text{ cm}$ is bent into a rectangle of width $x\text{ cm}$ and length $(12 - x)\text{ cm}$. Find the maximum area of the rectangle.
The volume $V\text{ cm}^3$ of an open container is given by $V = 12x^2 - 2x^3$ for $0 < x < 6$. Find the value of $x$ for which $V$ is a maximum.
The cost function $C$ for a can is modelled by $C = 2\pi r^2 + \dfrac{250}{r}$ for $r > 0$. Find the value of $r^3$ that minimizes $C$.
A curve models the profit $P = 150x - 5x^2 - 200$. By finding $\dfrac{dP}{dx}$ and $\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2}$, find the value of $x$ that maximizes $P$ and justify that it is a maximum.
For $0<t<6$, the length $L\text{ cm}$ is given by $L=3t(6-t)$. Find the value of $t$ for which $L$ is a maximum, and find this maximum length.
